NDT training in Nebraska: how it works for Nebraska employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training across Nebraska, from Omaha and Lincoln to Grand Island, Kearney, Norfolk and North Platte. Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET are taught live online or onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you against its written practice once training hours, documented experience, exams and a vision test are complete. There is no Atlantis training centre in Nebraska.

Nebraska is a large state with a spread-out industrial base, and that shapes how NDT training has to be delivered. A steel mill in Norfolk, a power station on the Platte, a rail maintenance shop in Lincoln or North Platte, a grain-processing plant in Columbus and an inspection contractor in Omaha all need qualified people, but rarely enough of them at one time, in one place, to justify sending a crew out of state for weeks. Live online theory removes the travel for the classroom portion, and onsite practical sessions put the instructor on your equipment, your specimens and your procedures. This section explains, method by method and step by step, how a Nebraska technician or employer gets from untrained to certified under SNT-TC-1A.

If your plan is already clear, request a Nebraska training quote with methods, levels, headcount and dates. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Nebraska

All courses follow the ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended practice, so the topic outlines and exam structure slot into your employer's written practice. Practical examples are chosen to reflect Nebraska work: rail wheels, axles and welded car structures; steel mill equipment and joist and deck fabrication; power-plant boilers, piping and condensers; pipeline and compressor-station welds; irrigation and utility-pole fabrications; and pressure vessels, ammonia systems and boilers in the ag-processing and ethanol sector.

MethodLevelsWhat Nebraska employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic testing (UT)I, II, III prepRail axle and wheel inspection, power-plant piping thickness surveys, structural weld examination on fabricated steelNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
Phased array UT (PAUT)IIPipeline girth welds, pressure-vessel welds and heavy fabrications where radiography disrupts productionUT Level II or equivalent
Time-of-flight diffraction (TOFD)IIFlaw sizing on thick-wall vessels, boiler headers and drums during outagesUT Level II
Radiographic testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipeline and piping weld radiography, castings, pressure-vessel seamsNone for Level I; radiation safety training and state requirements for field work
Magnetic particle testing (MT)I, IIRail components, forgings, crane and lifting equipment, structural welds on towers and polesNone for Level I
Liquid penetrant testing (PT)I, IIStainless food-processing equipment, non-ferrous castings, pump and valve componentsNone for Level I
Visual testing (VT)I, IIWeld visual on steel fabrication, boiler and vessel inspections, bridge and tank inspectionsNone for Level I
Eddy current testing (ET)I, IICondenser and heat-exchanger tubing at power stations and processing plants, aircraft surface inspectionNone for Level I

Ultrasonic testing. UT Level I covers wave theory, transducers, couplants, reference blocks, straight-beam and angle-beam technique and thickness gauging. Level II adds DAC and TCG, flaw location and sizing, and interpretation against code acceptance criteria. Nebraska has an unusually strong rail component: axles, wheels and welded car structures are routinely examined by UT and MT, and technicians who understand those geometries are valued by rail shops and contractors. Power-plant thickness surveys and structural weld inspection make up much of the rest.

PAUT and TOFD. Advanced UT at Level II covers focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoded data acquisition, TOFD set-up, analysis and reporting. For Nebraska contractors these skills open work on pipeline construction and repair, compressor station piping, and outage inspection at thermal plants, where clients increasingly prefer encoded UT to radiography.

Radiographic testing. RT courses cover radiation physics, isotope and X-ray sources, film and digital imaging, exposure technique, image quality and interpretation. Nebraska is an NRC Agreement State, so a company running field radiography needs a state licence, and individual radiographers must meet radiation safety and radiographer certification requirements; the course covers interpretation competence, not the licence.

MT, PT and VT. Surface methods are where most Nebraska NDT careers begin. MT covers yokes, prods, coils and bench units, wet fluorescent technique and demagnetisation, which matters for rail and heavy-equipment parts; PT covers solvent-removable and water-washable systems for stainless and non-ferrous components common in food processing; VT covers direct and remote visual, weld gauges and code acceptance criteria.

Eddy current. ET runs from electromagnetic theory and impedance-plane display through surface probes, bobbin-probe tube testing and conductivity measurement. It is used by outage contractors on condensers and feedwater heaters and by aviation maintenance.

Level III preparation. For senior technicians, ASNT Level III training prepares you for the Basic and method examinations, including procedure writing, technique approval and administering a certification programme, a skill in short supply across the state.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Nebraska, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is an employer-based scheme. There is no state NDT licence in Nebraska; your employer certifies you against its own written practice. The sequence is:

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer adopts a written practice defining the methods, levels, required training and experience, exam content and passing grades, and recertification rules.
  2. Classroom training. You complete the formal training hours set in the written practice for your method and level. Current figures are listed in the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. You work in the method under supervision and log the hours. Experience and training are separate requirements.
  4. General examination on method principles and theory.
  5. Specific examination on your employer's equipment, procedures, specifications and acceptance criteria.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens containing known discontinuities, administered and graded under the authority of a Level III.
  7. Vision examination: near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation, with near vision repeated annually.
  8. Certification signed by the employer, recorded and available for client audits.
  9. Recertification at the interval the written practice sets, by re-examination or documented continuing performance as permitted.

Our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide explains each step in more detail.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Nebraska crews

Distance is the defining factor in Nebraska. From Omaha to Scottsbluff is most of a day's drive, and many industrial sites sit well outside the two metro areas. Atlantis delivery reflects that:

  • Live online classroom. Instructor-led theory sessions that technicians in Kearney, Hastings, Columbus or the Panhandle can attend without travel. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. The instructor travels to your plant, rail shop, mill or yard, trains on your equipment and specimens, and can administer examinations under Level III oversight. For groups this is usually the most efficient model.
  • Blended. Online theory first, followed by a compact onsite practical block, which keeps people away from production for the shortest time.

We schedule around your operating year. Power stations plan spring and autumn outages; ethanol and processing plants have planned maintenance shutdowns; pipeline and construction work peaks in the warmer months; agricultural processors are busiest around harvest. Tell us your windows and we will plan training so certified people are ready before the work starts. Ask about onsite training for your Nebraska crew, or review corporate NDT training for multi-site programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Nebraska

Nebraska has no refinery and no shipyard, but it has a broader NDT market than its reputation suggests:

  • Rail. Union Pacific is headquartered in Omaha, and its Bailey Yard at North Platte is one of the largest rail classification yards in the world. BNSF also has a major presence, including shop operations in Lincoln. Rail car, locomotive and component maintenance uses UT, MT and VT heavily, and rail-car manufacturing in Lincoln adds welded-structure inspection.
  • Power generation. Nebraska is served entirely by public power. Nebraska Public Power District operates Cooper Nuclear Station near Brownville and the Gerald Gentleman Station near Sutherland; Omaha Public Power District operates the Nebraska City and North Omaha stations and is decommissioning the former Fort Calhoun nuclear station. Boiler and piping inspection to ASME Section I and B31.1 and nuclear in-service inspection to ASME Section XI drive UT, RT and ET demand, largely during outages.
  • Steel and fabrication. Nucor's steel mill and Vulcraft operations in Norfolk, Valmont Industries in Omaha and Valley, and Lindsay Corporation's irrigation manufacturing represent a significant welded-steel base: poles, towers, irrigation structures, joists and deck, typically fabricated to AWS D1.1 and inspected by VT, MT and UT.
  • Pipelines and gas transmission. Northern Natural Gas is headquartered in Omaha, and interstate crude and gas pipelines cross the state. Construction and integrity work follows API 1104, with RT, UT, PAUT and MT on girth welds and repairs, under federal PHMSA pipeline safety rules.
  • Agricultural processing, ethanol and fertiliser. Meat processors, grain processors, ethanol plants and fertiliser and ammonia storage operate boilers, pressure vessels, storage tanks and process piping that require periodic inspection, including ammonia refrigeration systems. UT thickness surveys, VT and PT on stainless equipment are common.
  • Aerospace and defence. Offutt Air Force Base near Bellevue hosts the 55th Wing and US Strategic Command, and the Nebraska Air National Guard flies from Lincoln. Aircraft maintenance NDT centres on ET, PT and UT, and military programmes often follow their own technical orders or NAS 410; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based.
  • Bridges and infrastructure. Nebraska Department of Transportation bridge work follows AWS D1.5 for welded steel, with UT and MT on fabrication and repair welds.

Radiography licensing in Nebraska. Nebraska is an NRC Agreement State, and radioactive materials licences, including industrial radiography, are administered by the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services through its radiological health programme. A company running gamma radiography in the field needs a state licence with an approved radiation safety programme and radiation safety officer, and individual radiographers must complete radiation safety training and hold a qualifying radiographer certification, working under two-person and monitoring rules at temporary job sites. Work inside the protected area of a nuclear plant also falls under the utility's NRC-licensed programme. X-ray equipment must be registered under state rules.

What Nebraska employers ask for. Typical requirements are ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT, MT or PT; RT Level II plus radiographer credentials for field radiography; conventional UT before PAUT; and, on nuclear work, the utility's specified programme, often ANSI/ASNT CP-189 with ASME Section XI rules and, for some UT, performance demonstration. Some fabricators also want an AWS CWI on staff for weld visual inspection, which is a separate credential Atlantis does not train.

Level III services and written practices for Nebraska NDT companies

Qualified Level IIIs are scarce in Nebraska, and many manufacturers and small inspection companies share or outsource the role. Atlantis provides outsourced Level III support that keeps your certification programme defensible:

  • Written practice development or gap review against the current SNT-TC-1A edition; see written practice development.
  • Procedures and techniques written to the codes your clients name, from AWS D1.1 and D1.5 to ASME and API 1104.
  • Examinations prepared, administered and graded under Level III authority, with audit-ready records.
  • Audit and pre-qualification support for utility vendor audits, rail customer audits, pipeline operator qualification reviews and ISO 9001 surveillance.

For the rules behind all of this, see SNT-TC-1A guidance. To talk through your programme, book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

Nebraska technicians often train on sites where spare equipment time is limited. Practical NDT, the Atlantis 3D simulator, lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods across five environments, including an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank, so set-up sequences and scan patterns become familiar before practical sessions on real equipment.

The simulator is practice only. It does not replace hands-on training, and it does not replace the practical examination, which must be carried out on real specimens and graded under Level III authority. For written exam revision, work through the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop writes the course material, provides Level III oversight of examinations and works directly with Nebraska employers on written practices and programme design.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Nebraska

How do I get NDT certified in Nebraska?

Nebraska has no state NDT licence. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after you complete classroom training, supervised experience, general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and a vision test. Starting with Level I training in UT or a surface method improves your chances with rail, fabrication and inspection employers.

Can I take NDT training online in Nebraska?

Yes. The theory portion is available as live online instruction anywhere in the state, which is how most technicians outside Omaha and Lincoln take it. Practical training and the practical exam still require real equipment and specimens, usually onsite at your employer. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and your existing training and experience. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom and experience hours for each level; the training requirements matrix lists them. Send us your logged hours and we will map what remains.

Do I need a license for radiography in Nebraska?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence or X-ray registration from the state, because Nebraska is an NRC Agreement State. Individual field radiographers need radiation safety training and a qualifying radiographer certification and work under the licensee's programme. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is a competence certification, not a radiation licence.

What does NDT training cost in Nebraska?

Pricing is quote on request, based on method, level, number of trainees, delivery format, travel for onsite work and whether examinations and Level III services are included. Quotes are returned within one business day: request a Nebraska quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Nebraska employers?

Yes. ASNT SNT-TC-1A is the framework most US industrial employers use, including rail, power, fabrication and inspection contractors in Nebraska. Because certification belongs to the employer, a new employer will review your records and may re-examine you.

Is there NDT work on the railroads in Nebraska?

Yes. Rail maintenance and manufacturing around Omaha, Lincoln and North Platte use UT, MT and VT on wheels, axles, bearings and welded structures. Railroads and their contractors often run their own qualification requirements on top of SNT-TC-1A, so confirm what the specific employer expects.

Can you train technicians at Cooper Nuclear Station or other power plants?

Nuclear in-service inspection is governed by the utility's programme and ASME Section XI, often with ANSI/ASNT CP-189 certification and performance demonstration for some UT. Atlantis training builds the SNT-TC-1A method foundation; confirm the exact requirement with the utility or its ISI contractor before enrolling.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Nebraska?

UT and MT are the most consistently requested because of rail, steel fabrication and power generation. VT is required almost everywhere welds are inspected. PAUT is increasingly asked for by pipeline and power contractors.

Can a Nebraska manufacturer certify its own NDT staff?

Yes, if it has a compliant written practice and a qualified Level III to administer exams and sign certifications. Many use an outsourced Level III; see written practice development.

What do NDT technicians earn in Nebraska?

Pay depends on method, level, sector and travel, and rail and outage work differ considerably. For sourced ranges, see the NDT salary guide 2026.
